职位介绍
作为 VALORANT Mobile 团队负责 Meta Systems 的产品经理 ，你将参与塑造玩家在每一场战斗前、战斗间隙以及战斗结束后的整体游戏体验。
你将负责的玩家体验系统包括但不限于局内外成长、社交功能、资产展示、组队体验、玩家身份表达，以及其他能够提升长期参与度的局外系统。你的目标是确保 VALORANT Mobile 不只是在对局内有出色的战术竞技体验，也能在对局外持续给玩家提供回归、连接、表达自我与长期成长的理由。
这个职位需要你具备强烈的玩家同理心、结构化的产品思考能力，以及将模糊玩家需求转化为清晰产品方向的能力。你将与我们的联合研发伙伴 Quantum Studio，以及 Riot VALORANT 团队、设计、工程、发行团队和其他 Riot 内部伙伴密切合作，定义功能目标，审核落地质量，并通过数据、研究与产品判断持续优化玩家体验。
在 Riot 中国办公室，你将加入一支由不同文化背景的专业伙伴组成的团队。我们共同热爱游戏，也始终坚持以玩家为中心。为了支持 Riot 在中国办公室的协作文化，我们不强调传统层级头衔。真正重要的是你所承担的责任、展现的自主性，以及最终创造的影响力。
职责描述
推动 VALORANT Mobile Meta Systems 的产品方向与落地支持，包括局内外成长、社交、组队、资产展示、玩家身份表达，以及其他局外玩家体验系统。
与光子工作室联合研发伙伴紧密合作，定义新功能与现有功能的产品目标、功能需求、用户流程、体验原则和验收标准。

s.h: 在开发周期中持续审核并优化联合研发伙伴的功能实现，确保最终玩家体验直观、精致，并符合 VALORANT 的产品质量标准。
s.t:
结合玩家行为数据、用户研究、竞品参考与产品判断，识别能够提升参与度、留存、社交连接和长期玩家动机的优化机会。
与 Riot VALORANT 团队、发行团队以及其他产品负责人合作，确保 Meta Systems 的方向与更广泛的 VALORANT 产品原则、版本规划、运营节奏和玩家需求保持一致。
支持不同版本中 Meta Systems 优化内容的规划和优先级排序，在玩家影响、研发成本、业务目标和交付时间之间做出合理取舍。
代表 VALORANT Mobile 玩家在 Meta Systems 领域提出清晰观点，确保相关功能既能服务核心战术射击玩家，也能兼顾更广泛的移动端玩家群体。
追踪功能上线后的表现与玩家反馈，并与联合研发伙伴和相关 Riot 团队一起制定可执行的后续优化计划。
基本要求
拥有 5 年以上产品管理、游戏运营、系统设计或长线运营游戏相关经验，有移动游戏经验者优先。
曾负责或参与过玩家体验系统，例如成长、社交、组队、个人资料、收藏、成就、任务、新手引导或其他与玩家参与度相关的系统。
具备良好的产品判断力和玩家同理心，能够识别玩家需求，并将其转化为清晰的产品需求和体验优化方案。
能够处理具有一定复杂度的产品问题，评估不同方案的取舍，并在明确约束下提出务实可行的解决方案。
具备良好的数据理解能力，能够使用参与度、留存、转化漏斗、社交行为或功能使用数据来评估产品表现并指导后续迭代。

AI models reshaping how our community creates, plays, and connects, all run on Compute Platform.

As Senior Product Manager, Compute Platform , you'll set the strategy and roadmap for Roblox's next-generation AI infrastructure: the rapidly growing fleet of GPUs and AI accelerators spanning Roblox core and edge data centers, and public cloud that decides how fast we can train, serve, and scale every model on the platform.

You'll own the products that turn raw GPU hosts into reliable, production-ready AI compute - driver and firmware management, fleet-wide health and performance, and the abstractions product teams across Roblox build on.

Drive strategy and roadmap for Compute Platform spanning Managed Kubernetes (Roblox Kubernetes Service), Managed Compute Services and other critical distributed systems, and our fleet of GPU and CPU machines managed via unified Fleet APIs - all across on-prem and cloud.
Drive the evolution of our Compute infrastructure to support Roblox’s most critical workloads - from AI to Storage to Data Analytics and more - each with their own distinct requirements.
Build and scale our GPU infrastructure to support training and inference for frontier models, enabling innovation at scale while optimizing cost-to-serve.
Stay laser-focused on Compute Platform Reliability for AI and other Roblox workloads, lowering mean-time-to-detection and recovery from failures.
Partner closely with seven key platform teams to understand their use cases and empower them with Compute Platform primitives enabling them to build on top easily.
Lead cross-functionally, acting as the connective tissue between Compute Platform Users, Engineers, AI researchers, Product, Finance, and Roblox leadership.

7+ years of product management experience, focused on Compute infrastructure or distributed systems at scale.
Deep practical understanding of Kubernetes internals and control plane components (API Server bottlenecks, Etcd scaling limitations, Kubelet behavior, etc) and experience productizing custom Kubernetes Operators, Controllers, and Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) to extend platform capabilities beyond vanilla implementations.
Deep familiarity with GPU/accelerator architecture and scheduling challenges, including topology-aware placement, preemption, hardware affinity constraints, and mechanisms to validate resource readiness before scheduling to avoid wasted compute cycles.
Familiarity with cloud-native service networking including microservices, CNIs, and enterprise-grade service mesh architectures.
Built production-grade compute platforms where efficiency, reliability, and developer experience were designed-in from day one.
The ability to balance the needs of multiple users and stakeholders and make optimal tradeoffs between utilization, latency, cost and time-to-ship while maintaining reliability.
A builder mindset - you are passionate about prototyping, evolving products through rapid iteration, and leveraging AI for ideation and unlocking value for users.
Experience building Compute infrastructure on AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Azure or other cloud providers. (preferred)
Background in AI model development, training, inference. (preferred)
Kernel-level experience or familiarity with custom kernel drivers. (preferred)
Experience building agentic systems for Compute or infrastructure. (preferred)

Utilize both quantitative and qualitative data to analyze the impact of product changes and iterate to improve key metrics.

Strong analysis skills, with hands-on experience defining KPIs, running experiments, and deriving actionable insights from a variety of sources

Passion for gaming, sandbox games, modding, and user-generated content and the communities that coalesce around them.
Hands-on experience developing game mods and in modding communities.

Truecaller's mission is to build trust in communication by making it safer, smarter, and more efficient. Born in Sweden, trusted by the world, and here’s why we stand out:
We are trusted by over 450 million active users every month across 190+ countries
We identify over 15 billion calls daily, helping users avoid spam and scams
We are powered by a team of 450+ employees from 45+ nationalities
We always look for people who take initiative, own their work, and keep raising the bar. An entrepreneurial mindset matters here, especially when it turns bold ideas into real actions. We stay collaborative and focused, always searching for smarter paths forward. If you want to make an impact and grow with a team that inspires millions, you’ll fit right in.

Truecaller's ads business reaches over 400 million users and is one of the largest in-app advertising platforms in its markets.

We are building a modern, server-driven programmatic stack that we own end to end, and this role owns the platform at the heart of it: the intelligence layer that powers demand-supply matching across all our demand channels.

Every ad opportunity flows through this platform, and it decides how that opportunity is valued, priced, auctioned, and allocated to maximize revenue while protecting user experience.
This is a senior, high-ownership role at the center of a multi-year platform build, working closely with engineering, data science, and the supply and demand product teams.

Own the platform strategy and roadmap: the decisioning, auction, and pricing systems that sit between our supply and our demand partners.
Build auction intelligence: bid landscape analysis, pricing and floor strategies, auction design, and demand orchestration that decides which demand sources to invoke for each opportunity.
Drive yield: deliver measurable improvements in eCPM, fill, win rate, and incremental revenue; identify revenue leakage and close it through platform enhancements.
Optimize for scale: drive initiatives around platform performance, reliability, and latency as traffic volumes and demand partners grow.
Shape the long-term architecture: capabilities like traffic shaping, audience-based packaging, and curated marketplaces that turn the platform into a durable competitive advantage.
Run a rigorous operating cadence: define platform KPIs and operational health metrics, design controlled experiments, and iterate based on measured impact.

6+ years in product management, with 3+ years in ad tech, programmatic advertising, or publisher monetization platforms. Hands-on experience driving revenue growth through programmatic is essential.
Programmatic depth: Strong understanding of the ecosystem, including unified auctions, header bidding, open bidding, mediation models, oRTB, and auction dynamics. Working knowledge of platforms such as Google Ad Manager, PubMatic, or ironSource.
Monetization fluency: comfort with the full KPI stack (eCPM, fill rate, match rate, win rate, bid density, viewability, ARPU) and a track record of using it to find and capture yield.
Platform product skills: proven experience building large-scale platform products with engineering-heavy teams, and the ability to translate complex business problems into scalable platform capabilities. Good understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and latency-sensitive architecture.
Data-driven rigor: strong analytical skills, comfort with large datasets, and fluency in experimentation, A/B testing, and controlled rollouts.
Stakeholder influence: ability to align engineering, data science, ad operations, and sales around a common platform strategy using data and business insight.

This Product Owner, PRM will work to design, manage, and build scalable solutions, specifically for how we manage, enable, and co-sell with our global partner ecosystem.

Bridge Business & Tech: Serve as the strategic liaison between the Partner teams and technical teams, ensuring all business requirements are fully documented, articulate the “what” and “why,” and are clearly understood by platform developers.
Map & Optimize Processes: Analyze and document "as-is" and "to-be" process flows to identify gaps, friction points for partners, and automation opportunities that can be converted into technical requirements.

Collaborate on Architecture: Partner closely with solution architects and development teams to design clean, scalable integrations between Salesforce.com, Impartner, and adjacent marketing automation or ERP technologies.
Drive End-to-End Delivery: Collaborate with end-users, technical squads, and change enablement teams from initial discovery through requirements gathering, build, user acceptance testing (UAT), and deployment.
Own the PRM Roadmap: Maintain a quarterly operational roadmap of enhancements for the partner experience, targeting increased channel efficiency, accurate pipeline reporting, and readiness for scale.
Measure What Matters: Set and track critical metrics for all initiatives. You know that a project doesn't end when a feature drops into production, but rather when partner adoption spikes and measurable operational targets are hit.

Ruby Labs is a leading tech company that creates and operates innovative consumer products. We offer a diverse range of opportunities across the health, education, and entertainment industries. We are looking for a highly organized Project Owner to own execution quality across one of our D2C subscription products. You will be fully responsible for keeping every workstream moving to standard - setting priorities with stakeholders, translating them into clear technical tasks, driving delivery across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing, and taking direct ownership of projects that have no dedicated owner.
This is a high-accountability role suited for someone who treats "almost done" as not done. We hold a high bar: clear tickets, honest timelines, and work shipped to standard. You will inspect the work, keep the team moving when pace or quality slips, and close gaps yourself when a project falls between roles.

Execution Ownership & Process
Set priorities together with stakeholders and maintain a single, agreed backlog
Own the delivery pipeline end to end, from prioritized backlog to verified release
Define and enforce processes, definitions of done, and quality standards across all workstreams
Drive sprint planning, task tracking, and follow-through so nothing stalls silently
Identify process bottlenecks and fix them with structure, not workarounds
Task Definition & Technical Clarity
Translate product and business priorities into precise, developer-ready technical tasks
Write specs with clear acceptance criteria, edge cases, and measurable outcomes
Partner with engineering to scope, estimate, and sequence work realistically
Use AI tools daily to accelerate spec writing, analysis, and QA - and spread what works across the team
Verify delivered work against spec before it ships — and reject what falls short
Standards & Team Accountability
Hold every contributor to explicit quality and deadline expectations
Push pace and raise the bar when execution drifts, directly and constructively
Run reviews and retros that convert misses into changed processes
Institutionalize best practices so quality does not depend on individual heroics
Cross-functional & Unowned Projects
Take direct ownership of initiatives that lack a dedicated owner and drive them to completion
Coordinate across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing to unblock dependencies
Collaborate with the Managing Director to align execution priorities with business goals
Keep stakeholders informed with concise, honest status reporting

Must-Have Experience
3+ years as a Project Owner, Product Manager, or Delivery/Project Lead on a live software product
Proven track record writing technical tasks and specs that engineers execute without back-and-forth
Experience running agile delivery processes (backlog management, sprints, releases) end to end
Demonstrated ability to build processes, checklists, and quality standards - not just follow them
Experience holding cross-functional contributors accountable for deadlines and quality
Working technical fluency: able to discuss implementation trade-offs with engineers credibly
Advanced, daily use of AI tools (LLMs, agents, AI-assisted workflows) to accelerate specs, analysis, and delivery - with command of standard task-management tooling (Jira, Linear, Notion, or equivalent)
Leadership Attributes
Highly structured operator - you build systems that make quality repeatable
Comfortable giving direct, specific feedback and enforcing standards without drama
Bias to ownership: picks up unclaimed problems instead of waiting for assignment
Detail-obsessed about the work itself - reads the ticket, tests the feature, checks the numbers
Clear, direct communicator who operates effectively in a remote environment
Location
Ruby Labs operates within the CET (Central European Time) zone. Applicants from any country are welcome to apply for the position as long as they are located within approximately ± 4 hours of CET. This ensures optimal collaboration and communication during working hours.

There is no one-size-fits-all career path at Thoughtworks: however you want to develop your career is entirely up to you. But we also balance autonomy with the strength of our cultivation culture. Responsible Use of AI in Recruitment
At Thoughtworks, we use AI tools to support our recruitment team with administrative tasks such as drafting communications, scheduling interviews and writing job descriptions.
Crucially, our AI tools do not screen, assess, rank or make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team and all selection decisions are made exclusively by our interviewers and hiring managers.
We are committed to fairness and responsible AI. We actively manage our AI systems by testing, monitoring for biased outcomes and implementing mitigation measures. We hold our third-party vendors to these same high standards through a rigorous governance process. For additional information, please see our full Thoughtworks AI Policy for Recruitment .

About Numan
Founded in 2018, we’ve already grown to be a 300+ team distributed across the globe, united by a singular mission: empowering people to take control of their health.
Numan is transforming health: we’ve built a cutting-edge platform that integrates diagnostics, medication, supplements, digital programmes, and doctor consultations. Giving people the tools they need to maximise life.
To deliver on our transformative mission, we are guided by our 5 company values:

· Patients first.

· Learn fast.

· Own the quality.

· Succeed together.

· Care deeply.
Backed by top-tier investors, Numan is already having a positive impact on hundreds of thousands of patients here in the UK, and we want you to help us deliver this mission!

This role is about taking our platform to the next level: moving toward sophisticated, predictive, and learning-based decisioning, with a clear path toward becoming a regulated medical device.
This is a senior, high-impact individual contributor (IC) role for someone who combines deep system understanding with clinical product judgement and real experience deploying AI/ML. You are AI-enabled, well-resourced, and measure your success by what you ship and move, rather than the size of your team. You move comfortably between high-level strategy and engineering-grade specifics.

Lead the product direction and roadmap for the decision platform, from long-term strategy down to the detail of how a rule actually works.
Decide which features and capabilities create the most scalable value, balancing near-term execution with strategic bets.
Establish and systematically track the success metrics for the platform.
Set the direction for how the platform uses AI and machine learning, embedding predictive and supervised learning systems into production.
Build self-learning systems so the platform continuously improves on its historical recommendations while keeping safety and explainability central.
Read and reason about system architecture. Act as a credible equal in technical debates with engineers, making sharp trade-offs between speed-to-value and long-term scalability.
Help shape the product side of the platform's regulatory direction, including the decision to build it as Software/AI as a Medical Device (SaMD).
Work fluently with sensitive patient data, partnering with clinical and quality colleagues to ensure safety and patient trust fundamentally shape the roadmap.
Proactively show engineering, clinical, design, and other product teams what the platform makes possible, while staying pragmatic about what they can absorb today.

A proven track record as a Senior or Principal Technical PM on complex platform, infrastructure, or systems products.
Hands-on experience deploying machine learning in production, specifically supervised learning or predictive systems.
Experience deploying or regulating software/AI as a medical device (SaMD), or working within closely comparable regulated frameworks.
Direct experience working with rules engines, knowledge graphs, or AI-driven decisioning systems.
Experience in clinical, healthcare, or adjacent domains handling sensitive, highly detailed user data.
Experience operating as a high-velocity individual contributor who leverages AI tools to cover ground that would traditionally require multiple people.

Prior experience working directly as a data scientist or software engineer before transitioning into technical product management.
Experience dealing with complex biological or personalized health data points.

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
AI agents are changing how everyone works — not just developers writing code, but entire organizations building, deploying, and operating software. Agents are becoming teammates: they write code, run tests, manage infrastructure, analyze data, and automate workflows across every function.

Docker is building a new platform from scratch to make this real — secure execution environments, agent-to-tool connectivity, governance controls, and the infrastructure that lets agents and humans collaborate safely at enterprise scale.
This is a 0-to-1 role. You will define the product strategy and own the roadmap for a new platform that sits at the intersection of AI, containers, and developer experience. You will work with a small, high-velocity team spanning engineering, design, and go-to-market to figure out what to build, ship it, learn from it, and iterate. The early signal is already in market — Docker Sandboxes is one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history — and the opportunity ahead is much larger.
We are looking for someone who builds, not just plans. You should be comfortable prototyping, getting your hands dirty with early product iterations, and improvising when things don’t go as expected. The right candidate has shipped developer tools or infrastructure products, understands how the agentic AI ecosystem is evolving, and thrives in the ambiguity of building something genuinely new.

Own the product strategy. Define the vision, roadmap, and success metrics for Docker’s AI & Agent Platform. Make hard tradeoff decisions about what to build, what to defer, and what to cut.
Build from zero. This is a new platform. You will define the product from the ground up — writing the first specs, prototyping with engineering, validating with customers, and iterating rapidly based on what you learn.
Drive from conception through delivery. Write requirements, work with engineering to scope and prioritize, ship iteratively, and measure outcomes. You don’t hand off specs and wait — you are in the details.
Define how pieces of the agentic ecosystem fit together. Agents need secure execution, tool connectivity, model access, governance, and observability. You will define how these capabilities compose into a coherent platform — and where Docker’s boundaries are.
Think beyond developers. Agents are becoming essential for everyone who builds, deploys, and operates software. You will ensure the platform serves the full range of people who need agents to succeed — from individual developers to platform teams to enterprise operators.
Define the developer experience. Work with design and engineering to ensure that our AI products are intuitive, powerful, and meet people where they are — whether in the CLI, IDE, or CI pipeline.
Collaborate across Docker. You will work cross-functionally to ensure coherent product experiences and go-to-market alignment.
Influence technical direction. Partner with engineering leadership on architecture decisions. You don’t need to write the code, but you need to understand the technical tradeoffs and have informed opinions about them.
Represent the customer. Engage directly with developers, enterprises, and partners. Bring their voice into every product decision.
Overcome blockers. When something is in the way — a missing integration, an unclear market signal, a technical constraint — you figure out a path forward. You don’t wait for someone else to solve the problem.

Experience . 10+ years of product management experience, with at least 5 years on developer tools, infrastructure, or platform products.
Deep technical fluency. You can read an architecture diagram, understand container and VM runtimes, and have a working knowledge of how AI agents, LLMs, and protocol-level tool connectivity work. You don’t need to be a hypervisor engineer, but you need to hold your own with one.
Proven ability to ship 0-to-1 products. You have taken a product from idea through launch in a fast-moving environment. You know how to operate when there is no playbook.
Builder mentality. You prototype, you sketch architectures, you test early ideas with customers before the spec is done. You are a doer, not just a thinker.
Strong product sense and UX instincts. You care about the developer experience at a deep level — from API design to CLI ergonomics to error messages.
Strategic thinking with execution follow-through. You can set a multi-year vision and also write the spec for what ships next sprint.
Comfort with ambiguity. This space is new and moving fast. You thrive when the answer isn’t obvious and you have to go find it.
Excellent communication. You can write a crisp product brief, present to executives, and debate technical tradeoffs with engineers — all in the same day.
Experience growing and monetizing products at scale. You have been part of taking a product from early adoption to meaningful revenue, and you understand the pricing, packaging, and go-to-market decisions that make that happen.

Experience building products in the containers, cloud-native, or DevOps space
Experience with AI/ML developer tooling or the agentic AI ecosystem
Contributions to open source projects
Experience building and scaling a business from zero to significant ARR
What You’ll Work With
We are building a new platform for agentic development. Docker Sandboxes — isolated execution environments for AI coding agents — is one of the first products in this platform and one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history. But this is just the beginning. The platform will grow to span multiple product areas as we define how agents and people work together at scale.

Work the interfaces. Collaborate with operations, service partners and peer product teams so that what you ship lands in the real workflows of agents and back-office teams.
Build for a regulated bank. Design compliance, auditability and client protection into every capability from the start.

Three or more years in product management, with at least one shipped product or major capability you owned end to end.
Experience with AI-powered, conversational or automation products — or a demonstrable, hands-on understanding of how LLM-based systems behave in production.

You’ll join a fully staffed engineering team ready to execute, and together you’ll make ecosystem interoperability a reason customers choose and stay with Lattice.
If you enjoy solving complex problems, shaping platform strategy, and working with great internal and external partners, you’ll love the impact you can have here. As a Lead Product Manager for MCP & AI Ecosystem, you will:
Own the MCP and AI ecosystem strategy. Not only decide what features and integrations to pursue, but what MCP and AI mean to Lattice and our customers. Become a thought leader on how AI should shape HR for the better.
Ship integrations that create leverage. Deliver new MCP tools, resources, and third-party connectors that expand what admins, managers, and executives can do with Lattice data in the flow of work.
Build durable foundations, like authentication, agentic execution frameworks, and evals that make future integrations faster, more scalable, and easier to adopt and maintain.
Be a technical thought partner to Engineering. Help shape technical direction on MCP tool design and third party integration infrastructure, translating complex constraints into clear product decisions.
Drive go-to-market with partners. Partner with Partnerships, Product Marketing, to launch integrations that deliver measurable customer and ecosystem impact.
Own outcomes. Influence and own key results across integration and MCP adoption, reliability, activation, and ecosystem growth.

We’re looking for a seasoned product manager with the technical depth and strategic instincts to shape Lattice’s next generation of integrations and APIs. You’ll be a great fit if you have a combination of:
7+ years of product management experience, with meaningful ownership of integrations, platform, or ecosystem surfaces (built end-to-end, not just configured).
Direct experience building technical integrations in a multi-party ecosystem — for example ad technology / marketing technology, marketplaces, developer platforms, payments, data connectivity, or similar — where partnership strategy shaped what you built.
Strong technical fluency: comfortable with third-party integration patterns, data sync and field mapping, webhooks, and auth/OAuth; you can hold a credible architecture conversation with engineers and partner CTOs.
A track record of shipping scalable, reliable integrations in partnership with engineering, and of standing up partner or marketplace launches with go-to-market teams.
Evidence of turning a platform or ecosystem into a competitive advantage — a reason customers chose your product, not just a checkbox.
Clear, confident communication that brings internal teams and external partners into alignment.
A bias for action and the ability to create structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving space.

Exposure to AI ecosystems, MCP, AI agents, or LLM tooling (helpful, not required).
Experience in multi-product B2B SaaS, or with HR/people-data or other sensitive-data workflows.

Translate complex accounting and fund finance requirements into clear product logic, automation, and audit trails.

Ensure end-to-end data integrity, from transaction ingestion through the ledger to downstream reporting and performance outputs.

We are building the world's decision infrastructure: the strategic twin of every industrial organization for complex combinatorial problems. You own the product and the priorities behind it. The hard part of that job here is structural: our go-to-market runs vertically, one use case at a time, while the product has to stay general enough to serve the next customer without being rebuilt.
You sit between Sales and Engineering and translate in both directions. Towards Sales: which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim. Towards Engineering: which requirement is ready to be built, what it needs to be complete, and what we deliberately leave out.
This is an early-stage role and we expect you to shape it rather than inherit it. We are extending the core of the application right now, which means your first decisions land while the product is still taking form. At the beginning, a meaningful part of your work will be spent on customer projects, close to the people whose decisions we model. That is where you see which patterns are worth turning into product.
We will not sugarcoat it: short deadlines, wild workload, and a go to market with the product and its tech that is a day to day focus and iteration process.
What you'll own
The product roadmap and the reasoning behind it: what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.
The boundary between standard product, configuration, and manual work for one customer.
Requirements that engineering can build from: scope, acceptance criteria, and a clear statement of what is out.
What we can credibly promise a customer, including where the product's limits currently are.
Proofs of Value that you run yourself, and responsibility for individual accounts.
Prototypes you build to test features with customers before we commit engineering time.
How product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
Your number: how much of what is project work today is standard product a year from now, and the time from a recognised customer problem to a usable capability.
This role is not for you if your strength is backlog, process and ceremonies, if you need research and design capacity before you can decide, if a complex industrial domain is an obstacle rather than the interesting part, if you don't like data or if you need more than three days before your first customer conversation.

A technical and analytical foundation, engineering, data analytics, data science, operations research, quantitative controlling, or finance with real modelling from a technical degree, technical consulting, or technical product management. You will not write production code, but you need to recognise when a requirement creates technical debt, or is built in a way that cannot be reused at the next customer.
5+ years in product management, or consulting with genuine product proximity. More important than the title: you have owned a product area end to end before, not only a backlog.
Experience deciding under incomplete information, and the ability to explain your trade-offs afterwards: what you chose, why, and what it cost.
You can sit with a plant manager or a controller, understand how they decide today, and leave the room knowing what the product has to do about it.
Good to have, not a cut off: optimization experience, deeper knowledge in manufacturing, supply chain or S&OP, enterprise B2B sales cycles involving operations, IT and controlling, or early-stage startup experience.
German C1 or higher, fluent in English.
NRW-based (Cologne office), optionally Munich, Stuttgart, Berlin area or else willing to work hybrid. Open to find a way if we fit.

Impact. You work with substance and lead what the product becomes.
Ownership. You define how product works here: what we build, what we decline, and where the boundary between product and project sits. No approval loops.
The people next to you. You work directly with the researchers and modellers, have access to tech deliveries and execute and build on eye level with the founders.
Exposure. You present your own roadmap and the reasoning behind it to the board, you sit in the core strategy conversations, and you stand in front of the people whose decisions we model.
Feedback speed. You will know directly what you are up to, we speak out loud, we adjust, we grow. Together.

SKALAR – Wir bauen die digitale Steuerkanzlei der Zukunft
Radikal einfach. Voll digital. 100% mandantenfokussiert.
Wir denken Steuerberatung komplett neu: einfacher, schneller und transparenter für Mandanten und Kanzleiteam zugleich.
Wo andere Kanzleien mit manuellen Prozessen, langen Wartezeiten und intransparenter Kommunikation kämpfen, bauen wir ein völlig neues Erlebnis - digital, proaktiv, KI-gestützt. Mit automatisierten Prozessen im Hintergrund und digitalen Schnittstellen zum Mandanten laufen repetitive Aufgaben weitgehend von selbst - damit du Zeit hast für das, was wirklich zählt: anspruchsvolle Beratung, Sonderfälle und strategische Mandantenfragen.
Der Unterschied zu anderen "Digitalkanzleien": Über die Hälfte unseres Teams sind Softwareentwickler. Du gestaltest direkt mit, was sie bauen - und damit, wie KI-gestützte Steuerberatung in dieser Branche überhaupt aussehen wird. Dein Steuerwissen prägt das Produkt, nicht nur dessen Anwendung.
Wir sind ein erfahrenes Gründerteam aus Steuerberatern, Digital-Unternehmern und Softwareentwicklern mit einem Exit-Track-Record von 140 Mio. €. Mit dir gemeinsam möchten wir eine der führenden Kanzleien Deutschlands aufbauen.
Deine Mission
KI-Features liefern, die Zahlen bewegen: Du verantwortest KI-Features end-to-end – Belegerkennung, Klassifizierung, automatisches Verfassen von Steuer-Antwortschreiben, RAG über Mandantenakten. Du baust die Eval-Frameworks, fährst die Prompt-Iterationen und triffst die Build-vs-Buy-Entscheidungen zu Modellen und Tooling. Keine Übergaben, keine Ausreden.
Werde besessen vom Nutzer: Du betreibst Discovery auf die harte Tour: Interviews, Shadowing-Sessions, Synthese von Rohfeedback. Du gehst tief genug, um echte von angenommenen Problemen zu unterscheiden – und wirst zur schärfsten Stimme des Nutzers in deiner Produktlinie.
Verantworte die Roadmap, verteidige die Trade-offs: Du verantwortest die Roadmap deiner Produktlinie end-to-end. Priorisierung über Geschäftswert, technische Machbarkeit und regulatorische Passung. Du kommunizierst Trade-offs klar an Engineering, Steuerberatung und Gründer – und verteidigst deine Entscheidungen mit Daten.
Halte die Messlatte beim Design: Du setzt einen hohen visuellen Standard und schützt ihn. Figma-Souveränität auf Review- und Skizzen-Niveau: Du entwirfst Flows, kritisierst Komponenten und blockst alles ab, was den Standard nicht erfüllt. Die beste Steuer-UX ist unsichtbar – mach unsere unsichtbar.
Laufe auf Daten, nicht auf Bauchgefühl: Du definierst die KPIs, die zählen – Time-to-Filing, Automatisierungsrate, Mandantenzufriedenheit, Berater-Effizienz – und steuerst jede Iteration aus Dashboards. Bauchgefühl bringt hier keine Features in Produktion.
Treibe die KI-Frontier: Du folgst der KI-Debatte nicht – du treibst sie. Evals, Prompt-Iteration, Kosten-Qualitäts-Trade-offs in Produktion. Du experimentierst unermüdlich mit dem Möglichen und bringst die Speerspitze ins Produkt.
Sei das Bindegewebe: Du sitzt zwischen Engineering, Steuerberatung und Mandanten und machst die Organisation dadurch schneller. First-Principles-Denken.
Dein Profil
Produkterfahrung: 3–6 Jahre Produktmanagement in B2B-SaaS, FinTech, Finance, Tax oder einem vergleichbar komplexen Umfeld. Du kannst auf Features verweisen, die du von der Vision bis zur messbaren Wirkung verantwortet hast – nicht auf Features, an denen du mitgewirkt hast.
KI-Track-Record: Mindestens ein KI-/LLM-Feature in Produktion ausgeliefert – mit echten Evals, Prompt-Iteration und Verantwortung für Kosten-Qualitäts-Trade-offs. Solides Verständnis moderner LLM-Stacks: RAG, Prompt Engineering, Fine-Tuning vs. In-Context-Learning, Vektor-Stores. ChatGPT-Prompts zählen nicht – wir wollen KI-native Workflows, die du tatsächlich gebaut hast.
Mandanten-Empathie, die sich übersetzt: Echte Empathie für beide Seiten – den Berater unter Fristendruck und den Mandanten, der einfach Sicherheit will – und die Disziplin, diese Empathie in Produktentscheidungen zu übersetzen, nicht in Backlog-Items.
Auge fürs Design: Figma-Souveränität auf Skizzen- und Review-Niveau. Klare Meinungen dazu, wie gute UI aussieht, und null Toleranz für schlampige Interfaces. Begeisterung für Claude Design ist ein Plus.
KI-Begeisterung: Du nutzt KI-Produkte täglich, kritisierst sie öffentlich oder privat und hast scharfe Ansichten dazu, wohin sie sich entwickeln. Praktische Vertrautheit mit Claude Cowork/Design/Code, GPT, Gemini o. Ä. ist die Baseline.
Selbst-Umsetzung: Du wartest nicht darauf, entblockt zu werden. Du prototypst, testest Prompts, verdrahtest Integrationen, hackst zusammen, was nötig ist. Wenn etwas blockiert ist, entblockst du es.
Strukturiertes Denken: MECE, First Principles, hypothesengetrieben. Du verdichtest Ambiguität zu klaren Entscheidungen – nicht zu weiteren Foliensätzen.
Kommunikation: Exzellentes Englisch (C2). Deutsch ist ein starkes Plus.
Domänen-Hintergrund: Erfahrung in Finance, Tax, Accounting oder angrenzenden Domänen ist ein starkes Plus – ebenso Vertrautheit mit Accounting-/Finance-Software-Stacks, DATEV, ELSTER oder regulierten Datenworkflows.

With Vista’s backing, we’re transforming from a successful UK business into a global scaling SaaS rocket ship, and we’d love for you to join us on our journey to £100M ARR across international markets.

Heidi operates across US, UK, Australia and beyond — and integrations are the connective tissue that makes it work everywhere. This PM role is a central platform function: the common layer through which every Heidi product (Scribe, Comms, Evidence) interfaces with the external systems clinicians already live in.
EMRs. Scheduling systems. Document stores. Clinical references. Secure messaging. Wherever clinicians already work, Heidi should plug in without making them think.
The integration stack is real and in motion: SMART on FHIR launches inside the chart, structured write-back into Epic, Cerner, Athena, MEDITECH Expanse, Veradigm, Best Practice. HL7 ADT feeds for patient demographics. Pre-charting from appointment data. The Integration Marketplace — surfacing Scribe, Comms and Evidence integrations in one place — is being rebuilt now, and you’ll own where it goes next.
You’ll own the integration framework, the customer-facing marketplace, and the roadmap that decides which connector ships next and how deep it goes. A small dedicated engineering squad sits alongside you. A new integration framework is rolling out. The marketplace is being unified across product lines. You’re picking up a running operation with strong opinions about where it goes.
Half your time is building the platform — the framework, the standards, the shared infrastructure every connector benefits from. The other half is customer-facing enablement: working directly with accounts, regional teams and commercial to get integrations live and keep them healthy.

The hard part is that every customer feels bespoke, three regional teams are always pulling in different directions, and real EMR behaviour rarely matches the spec. You’ll need to hold the line between configuring for one account and building for the platform.
You need to understand how a real EMR write-back actually works — encounter IDs, appointment IDs, patient context, addendum vs edit, side-by-side comparison, sectional mapping, the lookup tables that break in v1.0.2 of the desktop app.

You need to know when a customer request is a one-account fix and when it’s a framework change that touches every EMR. You need to be the person engineering trusts to call the build-vs-configure trade-off, and the person commercial trusts when they’re scoping integration requirements into a contract.

Über uns
Bei VREY bauen wir das EnergyOS für Mehrfamilienhäuser .
In Deutschland stehen über 3,3 Millionen Mehrparteienhäuser – und sie sind das schwarze Loch der Energiewende. <1% Solardurchdringung. <2% Smart Metering. Kaum Flexibilität oder intelligentes Energiemanagement.
Gleichzeitig zwingt die Regulierung Eigentümer zu massiven Investitionen: Solar wird zur Pflicht, Smart Meter müssen in den nächsten 5 Jahren flächendeckend ausgerollt werden, Heizung und Mobilität elektrifizieren sich. Das Mehrfamilienhaus wird vom Betongold zum aktiven Teil der dezentralen Energieinfrastruktur.
Was fehlt, ist ein integriertes System, das diesen Wandel wirtschaftlich und operativ beherrschbar macht.
VREY kombiniert zertifizierten Messstellenbetrieb mit eigener Software und ermöglicht Eigentümern erstmals, ihren selbst erzeugten Solarstrom direkt an ihre Mieter zu verkaufen – einfach und ohne selbst zum Energieversorger zu werden (§42b EnWG).
Damit wird regulatorischer Zwang zu einer profitablen und planbaren Chance:
Zweistellige Renditen und Wertsteigerung für Eigentümer,
~20 % Stromkostenersparnis für Mieter, und
digitale Infrastruktur für Speicher, Wärmepumpen und Flexibilität.
Bereits heute betreuen wir eine dreistellige Anzahl an Projekten - darunter die größten Bestandshalter und Wohnungsbaugenossenschaften - in allen 16 Bundesländern. Damit gehören wir nach kürzester Zeit zu den führenden Anbietern im Markt.
Im Zuge unserer Seed-Finanzierung haben wir 3,3 Mio. € von führenden Impact- und Energy-VCs (u. a. Rubio Impact Ventures, HTGF, Kopa Ventures) eingesammelt. Mit dem frischen Kapital gehen wir in die nächste Wachstumsphase und bauen unser Team gezielt aus.
Wir stehen am Anfang eines strukturellen Marktumbruchs. Wer heute die Energieinfrastruktur im Mehrfamilienhaus definiert, prägt sie für Jahrzehnte. Werde Teil von VREY und baue mit uns das führende EnergyOS.

When a contractor in Brazil gets paid on time, a business in Singapore settles in the right currency, or a payroll platform moves money to 40 countries without a single failure: that's what a good payments platform looks like from the outside. From the inside, it's hard decisions about which rails to build on, what reliability means at scale, and how to make a platform handling billions a month behave consistently across markets with completely different rules.
Nium processes cross-border payments for banks, fintechs, and enterprise platforms across 100+ countries. The Senior PM - Payments Platform owns the rails those payments run on.

Reliability. Define what "good" looks like for corridor performance, settlement success, and straight-through processing. Set the targets, own them, move them.

Corridor and market design . Each market has its own mechanics and failure modes. You translate that into requirements: what the corridor supports, how failure is handled, what go-live looks like, so the products built on top can make promises to customers and keep them.

Integration standards. You set the bar for what gets built with correspondent banks, local networks, and processors globally. You decide which integrations are worth doing, weighing partner economics and business impact against build and maintenance cost, and you push the ones that matter through to delivery.

Resilience. Design for failure: redundancy, failover, degraded modes. The goal is a platform where a single rail going down doesn't mean customers feel it.

AI and agentic payment flows . This is the frontier. Payments infrastructure today is reactive: something breaks, someone fixes it. We want infrastructure that thinks: routes intelligently, detects degradation before customers feel it, reconciles autonomously, resolves failures without human escalation. Nium wants to be the first payments infrastructure company to make agentic flows core to how money moves. You define what that looks like and build it.

Payments experience at real scale: high volume, multi-market, genuine accountability when things break. You understand the mechanics (settlement windows, return codes, reconciliation, failure handling) well enough to bring unambiguous requirements.

Curious about how payments work across markets. AI-native in how you work. Rigorous about prioritization. Opinionated, not passive: you form a point of view on how a corridor or integration should work, and you push it forward rather than waiting to be told what to build.

You push Engineering on trade-offs and bring them along with you, holding ground on what's right for the corridor and the business without needing positional authority to do it. And above all, you are passionate about the customer outcome at the end of the transaction, not the platform for its own sake.

3-5 years in product management. Payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure is a requirement. Experience with real-time rails (UPI, SEPA, RTP, Pix, or equivalents) is a strong plus.

The Opportunity

Most payments PMs work on one market, one rail, one product type. Here you work on all of them simultaneously: Asia-Pacific, Americas, Europe, MENA, all with different mechanics and failure modes. The exposure you get in two years compresses what usually takes a decade.

The team is small, senior, and ambitious. The infrastructure you build will process tens of billions of dollars a month and affect the finances of real people and businesses, including the first generation of payments that run through AI agents rather than human-initiated flows.

Corridor success rate and STP rate, moved quarter over quarter.

Settlement failure rate and time-to-resolution.

Integration delivery against committed dates.

Reduction in payment failures from platform-layer decisions.

Stäubli Electrical Connectors develops advanced connection technology and solutions based on the reliable MULTILAM contact technology. In the field of photovoltaics, Stäubli is a pioneer and world market leader with its MC4 connector system.

## Job Description ##
The Power Transmission & Distribution (PTD) division of our Electrical Connectors Division provides innovative interconnect and contact solutions for critical power applications.

The focus is on enabling reliable, efficient and high-performance energy transmission, distribution and supply, in power grids, energy plants, data centers and industrial applications.

Driven by global drivers such as electrification, AI and digitalization, we support the modernization of infrastructure and the growing global demand for high power density, efficiency and system reliability. As Head of Product Management, you will play a key role in our growth strategy.

· Working closely with sales, business development, R&D, marketing, and customers worldwide to further develop the market and establish and expand key relationships

· Degree in engineering (e.g. electrical engineering, mechanical engineering) or business administration with a strong technical understanding
· Several years of experience in product management, sales, product development or project management in an industrial environment
· In-depth knowledge of the development and management of product portfolios as well as the international market environment
· Experience with ERP (e.g. SAP), CRM (e.g. Aurea) and Office 365 systems
· Strong leadership and communication skills with the ability to motivate and strategically align teams
· High customer and market orientation as well as strong analytical and networked thinking
· Independent, structured and solution-oriented way of working with a willingness to travel internationally (~15%)
· Fluency in English is required; fluency in German and other languages are an advantage
